back: The cycle from one heat to the next: about 21 days in the cow, sow and doe; about 17 days in the ewe.
The short period when the female will stand to be mated; ovulation follows soon after it ends.
Cow 283 days; sow 114 days (3 months, 3 weeks, 3 days); ewe and doe 150 days; rabbit 31 days.
The oviduct (Fallopian tube); the embryo then implants in the uterus.

front: Why the testes are in the scrotum
back: Sperm production needs a temperature a few degrees below body temperature.

front: Surest sign of heat in a cow
back: Standing still when mounted by other cows or the bull (standing heat).
Cow seen on heat in the morning: serve that afternoon; seen in the afternoon: serve next morning.
Proven sires, no bull to keep, less venereal disease; needs accurate heat detection, a trained inseminator and stored semen.
Days from calving to conception + 283 days of gestation; for one calf a year a cow must conceive within about 82 days of calving.
